name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (fd2_ prefix + verb 'set' + descriptor 'chapter_init_done_flag') and matches the single global it writes (data_fd2_chapter_chapter_init_done_flag). No Ghidra address residue in the name. Mechanically accurate: the body's sole effect is setting that flag byte to 1.
purpose: Unconditionally sets the chapter_init_done_flag byte (@ 0x53A44) to 1.
logic_summary: Body is a compiler-injected __CHK(0x20) stack probe (no real locals) followed by MOV byte [0x53A44],1; RET. The only semantic effect is writing 1 to data_fd2_chapter_chapter_init_done_flag. The flag has exactly one reader and one writer (verified via xrefs): written here, and read only by the loop condition of `while (flag == 0) fd2_set_chapter_init_done_flag();` in fd2_game_main_loop on the action/confirm (Space 0x39 / Enter 0x1C) key path, entered only when click_debounce_skip_count == 0. Since the flag is BSS-cleared at load and this setter always writes 1, the loop body runs exactly once on the first qualifying confirm press (latching 0 -> 1); subsequent confirm presses skip it.
comment_original_issue: Both the src one-liner and the Ghidra plate were factually correct on the write, but the plate overstated the read side: it claimed the flag is 'read elsewhere by frame/loop state checks' and 'gates the one-time transition out of chapter init into active gameplay'. Xrefs to 0x53A44 show exactly one reader (the spin-loop condition in fd2_game_main_loop) and one writer (this function); there is no 'elsewhere' reader, so that broader gating narrative is not supported by evidence.
notes: The `while (flag == 0) setter();` idiom is not a bug: the setter unconditionally writes 1, so the loop is guaranteed to terminate after one iteration. Renaming the global (note the awkward doubled 'chapter_chapter' in data_fd2_chapter_chapter_init_done_flag) is out of scope for this function symbol and would be a Stage 2 concern; this function's own name is correct and kept. The global declaration comment block (lines 478-487) repeats the same overstated 'gate the transition into active gameplay' wording but belongs to a different symbol and was left untouched per single-symbol scope.
